title: Friday night ER load in Larkfield
question: Which emergency department gets overwhelmed first, what do patients actually want, and how many leave without being seen?

nodes.name: St. Brigid's Regional
nodes.about: Level 1 trauma and heart center; best reputation in the region; famous for long ER waits

nodes.name: Larkfield General
nodes.about: Community hospital ER; mixed reviews; posts its wait time online

nodes.name: Children's Medical
nodes.about: Pediatric ER only; parents rave about it

nodes.name: Lakeside Urgent Care
nodes.about: Urgent care with x-ray on site; cannot handle emergencies

nodes.name: Westfield Walk-in
nodes.about: Cheap walk-in clinic in a strip mall; basic care only

archetypes.name: Critical (chest pain, trauma)
archetypes.description: Need a full ED; ambulance or rushed drive.

archetypes.name: Moderate adult
archetypes.description: Fever, abdominal pain, breathing trouble; picks the hospital they trust.

archetypes.name: Minor injury
archetypes.description: Cuts, sprains and colds; checks wait times on their phone.

archetypes.name: Parent with child
archetypes.description: Heads for pediatric care if it is anywhere close.

minds.name: Dana Whitfield
minds.bio: Crushing chest pain while cooking dinner; her husband is driving.
minds.social: husband insists on St. Brigid's because "they have the heart people"

minds.name: Robert Haines
minds.bio: Fell off a ladder; possible broken hip; neighbor is driving him.
minds.social: neighbor is a retired nurse who has opinions about every hospital

minds.name: Kevin Osei
minds.bio: Motorcycle crash with a deep leg laceration; friends drove him.
minds.social: friends are checking wait times on their phones

minds.name: Grace Liu
minds.bio: Severe abdominal pain for six hours; a nurse friend said it could be appendicitis.
minds.goal: Be seen somewhere that can do surgery
minds.social: texts her nurse friend before every decision

minds.name: Samuel Okafor
minds.bio: Dizzy and short of breath; his wife once waited nine hours at Larkfield General.
minds.goal: Go to St. Brigid's, nowhere else
minds.social: daughter on the phone is begging him to go to the closest ER

minds.name: Tanya Brooks
minds.bio: Migraine with vision changes; terrified it is a stroke.
minds.social: sister is driving and will go wherever Tanya says

minds.name: Maria Gonzalez
minds.bio: Diabetic with an infected foot wound; must be at her night shift by 11pm.
minds.social: coworker said urgent care can handle infections

minds.name: Ahmed Karim
minds.bio: Kidney stone pain; St. Brigid's treated him for the same thing last year.
minds.goal: Pain relief as fast as possible

minds.name: Nia Thompson
minds.bio: Asthma flare and her inhaler is not helping; kids are home with a neighbor.
minds.social: neighbor texts every 20 minutes asking when she'll be back

minds.name: Luis Moreno
minds.bio: Sprained ankle at Friday soccer; no insurance.
minds.goal: Find out if it is broken without a huge bill
minds.social: teammates in the group chat share where they got seen

minds.name: Eli Navarro
minds.bio: College student who cut his hand on broken glass at a party.
minds.goal: Stitches and back before anyone notices
minds.social: drunk friends keep changing their minds about where to go

minds.name: Hannah Price
minds.bio: Bad sore throat; flying out for a wedding tomorrow morning.
minds.social: picks wherever the posted wait is shortest

minds.name: Frank DiMarco
minds.bio: Twisted knee gardening; on Medicare; has all night.
minds.social: his doctor told him to use urgent care for anything non-urgent

minds.name: Priya Raman
minds.bio: Toddler with a 104°F fever and a new rash.
minds.social: local parents' Facebook group swears by Children's Medical

minds.name: Jason Miller
minds.bio: Son, 8, broke his wrist at a trampoline park.
minds.social: wife says urgent care is fine for a wrist

minds.name: Chloe Bennett
minds.bio: Infant wheezing and struggling to breathe.
minds.social: nurse hotline told her to go to the nearest ER
